text:
Lina Gomez: Quick heads-up — I'm planning to relocate from Austin, TX -> Mexico City around Aug 1. Need clarity on payroll change, WFH stipend (do I keep US stipend?), equipment reimbursement, and whether this creates any tax/registro obligations for Redwood in Mexico.

Taylor Reed: Congrats! :tada: From People Ops: please update your address in Workday, fill out the International Remote Request form, and select expected move date + whether this is temporary vs permanent. Stipend is prorated by calendar month while location changes.

Lina Gomez: Thanks. What does "registro" mean here? Will the company need to register in Mexico?

Samir Patel: Short answer: possibly. If you're an employee working in MX long-term, local payroll and employer obligations (IMSS, employer social contributions) could apply. We typically open a case with our global payroll partner when someone moves to a new country for >6 months.

Ivy Lee: I'm supportive of the move. Happy to formalize approval — Lina, can you paste your tentative lease or travel dates into the form?

Lina Gomez: Lease is tentative for now (arrive Aug 1, 2-month Airbnb while I search). Will upload once I have it.

Taylor Reed: Equipment: if you need shipping or additional monitor/adapter purchases, submit receipts after purchase. Relocation reimbursement is discretionary — include justification on the relocation request.

Benefits Bot: FYI — US medical plans usually handle emergencies overseas only. For Mexico long-term we usually switch to local-compliant coverage or a global expat plan; dental/vision separate. Submit expected stay length so Benefits can run quotes.

Samir Patel: Bank/payroll: Do you want to stay on US payroll and receive USD direct deposit, or switch to MX payroll/ MXN? Staying on US payroll can be possible short-term but may trigger additional tax reporting and could create withholding complexities. Let payroll know preference in the form.

Lina Gomez: I'll stay on US account initially but likely switch to MXN after 3-4 months.

TaxBot: Heads-up: employee location can create corporate tax and permanent establishment risk depending on activities (client-facing work, contracting, hiring). We'll escalate to Tax & Legal once you submit the form. Avoid negotiating local contracts or hiring vendors on behalf of Redwood until Legal signs off.

Ivy Lee: Noted. Lina — please pause any local sales outreach or partner meets until Tax gives the go-ahead.

Lina Gomez: Understood. One more — WFH stipend: does the amount change by country?

Taylor Reed: Stipend rate is consistent company-wide, but currency conversion can affect take-home value. For long-term location changes we review on a case-by-case basis. If you change payroll country, stipend payments may also switch currency. We'll confirm in your case.

Samir Patel: Action items for Lina: 1) update Workday address, 2) complete International Remote Request with move date and bank preference, 3) upload lease/itinerary, 4) note any equipment requests. People Ops/Payroll/Benefits/Tax will triage after submission.

Lina Gomez: Thanks everyone — I'll fill out the form today and tag Ivy. Appreciate the quick answers! 

TaxBot: Reminder — submit form 7 days before move to allow tax review.

Taylor Reed: And ping me once done so I can start benefits/relocation conversations. :+1:
